analysis.title: Deleveraging Alert: Strongest Two Day Long Selling of US Hyperscalers Triggers Model
key_insights: Hedge funds sold down US Hyperscaler long positions on Wednesday and Thursday faster than in any two day period since COVID.
Total US net selling was made larger by long sales in Retailing and Capital Goods, plus a modest amount of long selling in Semis.
1.9% of US gross market value (GMV) was long sold across Wednesday and Thursday. 1.5% of GMV, about three quarters of that, was Hyperscaler long sales alone.
The speed of the move re-activated UBS's Deleveraging Indicator as of Thursday's close.
Equity long/short US portfolios are down an estimated 2.6% this week and 6.7% month to date as of Thursday's close.
The Deleveraging Indicator is not currently active in Europe or Japan.
Per the weekly PrimeView recap, hedge funds are becoming more selective with AI positions, adding shorts to cut AI beta and turning toward stock picking.
risk_factors: Continued hedge fund deleveraging in US Hyperscalers, with the Deleveraging Indicator now active.
Losses in L/S portfolios (-6.7% month to date) could prompt further position cuts.
vol_and_positioning: Hedge fund long selling in US Hyperscalers over Wed/Thu was the fastest two day pace since COVID, with 1.5% of US GMV sold in Hyperscaler longs alone.
UBS's Deleveraging Indicator is active for the US as of Thursday's close, and not active in Europe or Japan.
Equity L/S US portfolios are down an estimated 2.6% on the week and 6.7% month to date.
Hedge funds are adding shorts to reduce AI beta, shifting toward stock picking rather than broad AI exposure.
